hierarchy.evidence: Studio B appears first at both widths, but its small “6 min late” badge draws less attention than the illustrated title.

spacing.evidence: The cards align room names on the left and status badges on the right, while the compact desktop filter expands to the card width on mobile.

typography.evidence: The italic “rooms” distinguishes the title from the upright serif room names, and the bold sans-serif filters and statuses stay legible on mobile.

color.evidence: Plum and gold establish the theatre setting, while the amber clock and delay badge distinguish Studio B from Hall A’s green check and “Ready” badge.

accessibility.evidence: Both browser trees identify the selected filter and pair each room heading with its status, though the filter button names omit the visible counts of 2 and 1.

fidelity.evidence: Both widths show Studio B as “6 min late” and Hall A as “Ready,” with “Delayed” and “All rooms” controls above the list.

hierarchy.evidence: At both widths, the prominent “6 minutes late” cell draws the eye directly to Studio B’s row, with “Delayed only” immediately above the table.

spacing.evidence: The filter aligns with the table’s left edge at both widths, and the mobile rows give the two-line delay label enough space to stay clearly grouped with Studio B.

typography.evidence: The serif title shifts from one line on desktop to two on mobile, while bold sans-serif status text remains easy to distinguish from the large serif room names.

color.evidence: White text on burgundy singles out the delay, a green check marks “Ready,” and the dark fill identifies the selected “All rooms” filter.

accessibility.evidence: Both browser trees associate each status cell with a room row header, mark “All rooms” as pressed and expose “2 of 2 rooms” as a status.

fidelity.evidence: Both views label the controls “Delayed only” and “All rooms” and show the exact pairings of Studio B with “6 minutes late” and Hall A with “Ready.”

hierarchy.evidence: The drawing leads into the product name, $46 price and prominent “Add to bag” button on desktop, and mobile preserves that reading order in a single column.

spacing.evidence: A generous desktop gutter separates the drawing from the details, while the mobile image, copy and full-width button share a left edge, with shipping tucked just below the button.

typography.evidence: The upright and italic product name scales cleanly from two lines to one, though the tiny uppercase “Small-batch pottery” label takes effort to read at 390 px.

color.evidence: Clay red connects the studio mark, italic “Bowl” and purchase button, whose white lettering stands out against the dark fill at both widths.

accessibility.evidence: At both widths the browser tree names the visible controls “Bag, empty” and “Add to bag” and includes a status region and image text describing the speckled glaze and brown rim.

fidelity.evidence: The bowl drawing, $46 price, Milwaukee throwing and glazing details, “Ships in 5 days” and “Add to bag” match the brief, with post-add confirmation unverified in the supplied empty-bag views.

hierarchy.evidence: The drawing and large product name identify the bowl immediately, and pairing $46 with the plum “Add to bag” button makes the purchase action easy to find at both widths.

spacing.evidence: The desktop divider and even spacing group shipping with the purchase row, while roughly 150 px of empty space separates them on mobile.

typography.evidence: The two-line desktop title fits on one legible line on mobile, and the bold serif price and emphasized “5 days” make the buying details easy to scan at either width.

color.evidence: The ochre drawing and cream background give the page warmth, and the deep plum fill singles out the white purchase label at both widths.

accessibility.evidence: At both widths the visible zero count corresponds to “Bag, 0 items” in the browser tree, which also exposes a level-one product heading, a named drawing, an “Add to bag” button and a status region.

fidelity.evidence: Kiln & Field’s illustrated Oat Glaze Bowl has the requested $46 price, Milwaukee maker credit, five-day shipping and “Add to bag” action, with confirmation unverified because both captures show zero items.
